title: Tinned goods and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
text:
Published 20 November 2026, 07:26 GMT

Retail sales rose in October, driven by people buying long-life food such as tinned goods and UHT milk, according to official figures.

Sales volumes were 0.7% higher as people responded to the government's emergency preparedness "Be Ready" campaign.

This encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.

Separate research released last week suggested that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.

The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.

Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.

Meanwhile, separate official data showed the government borrowed slightly less than economists had expected in October.

Borrowing - the difference between public sector spending and income - was £17bn last month.

Although that was £0.8bn higher than October last year, it was below analysts' forecasts of about £18bn.
